This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.90,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of death of Ramod Sah, who is husband of petitioner No.1, father of petitioners No.2 to 4 and son of petitioner No.5, in a road traffic accident.
2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
The deceased Ramod Sah was working as a Fabricator/Welder Coolie under the builders of Prestige Golf Square, near Devanahalli.
On 18-04-2022, the said builders hired the Goods Vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-54-6940 to bring 'L' angles from Bengaluru for construction purpose.
They sent the deceased to bring 'L' angles in the said goods vehicle.

After loading 'L' angles in the vehicle, the Kusum Kumari vs Rizwan Pasha on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15880027/
2 deceased was sitting in the body of the said vehicle by holding 'L' angles.

sentences.text: The 'L' angles were negligently loaded in the said vehicle, in such a way that it had gone 3 feet upwards outside the said vehicle.
The said vehicle was driven by its driver from Kamakshipalya, Bengaluru, towards Prestige Golf Square.
On the way, at about 1.30 p.m., the said vehicle reached Neeleri Railway Gate on Nandi Hills Road, Devanahalli, Bengaluru Rural District.
The driver of the said vehicle drove the same with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, due to which the 'L' angles loaded in the said vehicle dashed against the road side tree branches.
Due to the said impact, the deceased has sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was taken to Manasa Hospital, Devanahalli, wherein the doctors declared him as brought dead.
Earlier to the accident the deceased was working as welder and bar bender and he was earning a sum of Rs.60,000/- per month.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
The BIAL Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said goods vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 304(A) of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.90,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
He has denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased.

He has contended that, on the alleged date of accident, he was driving his Ashok Leyland Goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA- 54-6940 on Nandi Hills road, slowly and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations.
When the said goods vehicle reached near Neeleri Railway Gate, Devanahalli, due to heavy wind the branches of road side tree suddenly fell on the front portion of the vehicle and accident occurred.
Further it is contended that, he is the R.C. owner of the said Ashok Leyland Goods vehicle.

The R.T.O. and such other documents pertaining to the said vehicle are standing in his name and the said vehicle was insured with the respondent No.2/Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., vide Policy No.76522123340001812, valid from 14-12-2021 to 13- 12-2022.

The policy was in force as on the date of accident and the respondent No.1 was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle, vide driving licence No.KA 18 19870000071, valid from 26-04-1987 to 14-12-2025.
If this Court comes to conclusion of granting compensation to the petitioners, the respondent No.2/insurance company itself is liable to pay the same.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Likewise, the respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has contended that, the deceased Ramod Sah was working as a fabricator/welder coolie under the builders of Prestige Golf Square, near Devanahalli.
Though the alleged accident is said to have been taken place during the course of employment, no claim petition is filed under the ECA Act against the builders of Prestige Golf Square.
The said builders are not made parties to the present petition.
Hence, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary and proper parties to this case.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance Kusum Kumari vs Rizwan Pasha on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15880027/
3 policy in favour of respondent No.1, in respect of Ashok Leyland Goods vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-54-6940 vide policy No.760522123340001812, valid from 14-12-2021 to 13-12- 2022.
It has denied the occurrence of the accident and death of the deceased was due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident.

Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1,
as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that, the deceased Ramod Sah S/o Shivkumar Sah has succumbed to the injuries sustained in vehicular accident, alleged to have been occurred on 18-04-2022 at about 1.30 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-54-6940 ?

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?

REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioners that, the deceased Ramod Sah was working as a Fabricator/Welder coolie under the builders of Prestige Golf Square, near Devanahalli.

11. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 has got examined herself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein she has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of their oral evidence, the petitioners have got marked total 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of notice, Ex.P.4 is true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.5 is true copy of sketch, Ex.P.6 are true copy of witness statements (total 8), Ex.P.7 is true copy of inquest, Ex.P.8 is true copy of post-mortem report, Ex.P.9 is true copy of notice U/Sec. 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.10 is true copy reply to the notice U/Sec. 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.11 is true copy of endorsement, Ex.P.12 is true copy of charge-sheet and Ex.P.13 to 18 are notarized copy of Aadhar cards of deceased and petitioners No.1 to 5.
12.

On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 12, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to negligently carrying the 'L' angles in the offending Ashok Leyland goods vehicle bearing No.KA-54-6940 and due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of said vehicle.

Further it reveals that, the 'L' angles were negligently loaded in the said vehicle, in such a way that it had gone 3 feet upwards outside the said vehicle, which came in contact with the road side tree branches, consequently causing grievous injuries to deceased Ramod Sah and resulting in his death.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet,
which is marked as Ex.P.12, has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Ashok Leyland goods vehicle bearing No.KA-54-6940 and negligently carrying 'L' angles in the said vehicle.

13. At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of offending Ashok Leyland goods vehicle bearing No.KA-54- 6940 in the said accident,
issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

But, the respondents No.1 and 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific contention that, there was no negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle and the same has been falsely implicated by the petitioners in collusion with the respondent No.1 and the jurisdictional Police.
But, the respondents have failed to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of R.W.1/respondent No.1 and R.W.2/representative of respondent No.2 insurance company, there is absolutely no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, there was no negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle/respondent No.1 and the offending vehicle has been falsely implicated by the petitioners in collusion with the respondent No.1 and the jurisdictional Police.
On the other hand, the R.W.1 has Kusum Kumari vs Rizwan Pasha on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15880027/

5 clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, he was carrying 'L' angles in the offending vehicle and the same were loaded in such a way that it had gone 2.5 to 3 feet upwards outside the said vehicle and the same came in contact with the road side tree branches.
Further he has unequivocally admitted that, the deceased was sitting in the back cabin by holding the said 'L' angles.

Further, the R.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, at the time of accident the offending vehicle was hired by the builders of Prestige Golf Square, Bengaluru, for transportation of construction materials.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by petitioners clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to negligently carrying the 'L' angles in the offending Ashok Leyland goods vehicle bearing No.KA-54-6940 and due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of said vehicle.

Though the learned counsel for respondents No.1 and 2 have cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her evidence or falsifies her case.

Further, the P.W.1 has unequivocally denied the suggestion made in her cross-examination that, there was no negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle and her husband has died due to health issues and not due to accidental injuries as alleged by them.

14. Further, the Ex.P.4 spot mahazar and Ex.P.5 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of 25 feet wide Nandi Hills road, near Neeleri Railway Gate, Nandhi Hills road, Devanahalli, Bengaluru District, due to coming in contact of negligently loaded 'L' angles in the offending Ashok Leyland goods vehicle bearing No.KA-54-6940 to the road side tree branches.
Further it is not case of the respondents that, the accident has occurred due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident has not taken place due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the deceased,
then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondents to disprove the case of the petitioners and even nothing has been brought out in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has occurred due to negligence of the deceased or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

15. Further, the Ex.P.8 Post-mortem report clearly speaks that, the deceased Ramodh Sha has died due to multiple organ injury with hypothalamic shock as a result of injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.

The investigation officer in his Ex.P.12 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Ashok Leyland goods vehicle bearing No.KA-54-6940 and the deceased has sustained grievous injuries on his chest and stomach and succumbed to said injuries.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the respondent No.1, who is the owner/driver of offending vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, with regard to date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending Ashok Leyland goods vehicle bearing No.KA-54-6940 in the said accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to deceased Ramod Sah in the said accident and the cause of his death.

19. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue, for the reasons stated therein, this Court has already held that, the petitioners have successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that,
the accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Ashok Leyland goods vehicle bearing No.KA-54-6940 and deceased Ramod Sah has succumbed to grievous injuries sustained in the said accident.
Now the petitioners are required to establish that, they are the legal representatives of the deceased.
In this regard, they have produced their respective Aadhar cards and Aadhar card of deceased Ramod Sah, which are marked as Ex.P.13 to 18.
The said documents clearly goes to show that, the petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioners No.2 to 4 are the children and petitioner No.4 is the father of deceased Ramod Sah.

On the other hand, the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased Ramod Sah is not specifically denied by the respondents and even there is no rebuttal evidence produced by them with respect to same.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the above documents produced by the petitioners and hold that, the petitioners are the legal representatives of deceased Ramod Sah.

20. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356, has clearly held that, "The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166(1).

sentences.text: The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependant on the deceased, would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.
This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra) had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.

sentences.text: It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."

21. According to the ratio laid down in above decision, the legal representatives though not fully dependent on the deceased are entitled to claim compensation under all the heads i.e., under both conventional and non-conventional heads.

In order to determine the compensation, the age,
avocation, income, dependency, future prospects of the deceased and other conventional heads are to be ascertained.
22. The compensation towards loss of dependency:

The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly established that, the petitioner No.1 being the wife, petitioners No.2 to 4 being the children and petitioner No.5 being the father of deceased Ramod Sah are the legal representatives of the deceased and they were depending on the income of the deceased.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
In order to calculate the loss of dependency, the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
i) Age and income of the deceased: The petitioners have averred that, the age of deceased as on the date of accident was 32 years.
To substantiate this point, the petitioners have produced the Aadhar card of deceased Ramodh Sah, which is marked as Ex.P.13, wherein the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 01-01-1990.
Admittedly, the accident has occurred on 18-04-2022.
Therefore, as on the date of accident the age of the deceased is considered as 32 years.
The petitioners have stated that, as on the date of accident the deceased was hale and healthy and he was working as welder and bar bender and was earning Rs.60,000/- per month.
But, the petitioners have not produced any document to show that, the deceased Ramodh Sah was working as welder and bar bender and was earning Rs.60,000/- per month.

In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court,
except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

a) The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the cases of, G. T. Basavaraj V/s Niranjan and another, in MFA No.7781/2016, judgment dated 11-08-2022, Ramanna and another V/s Y. B. Mahesh and another in MFA No.140/2017, judgment dated 16-01-2020 and New India Assurance Co. Ltd., V/s Anusaya and others in MFA No.101195/2014, judgment dated 05-01-2023, has clearly held that,
"when the income of the deceased is not proved, then the notional income as per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is to be adopted as the income of the deceased."

26. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of offending Ashok Leyland goods vehicle bearing No.KA-54-6940.

As per Ex.R.2 insurance policy, the offending Ashok Leyland goods vehicle bearing No.KA-54-6940 was insured by respondent No.2 insurance company, vide Policy No.760522123340001812, valid from 14-12-2021 to 13-12- 2022 and as on the date of accident the policy was valid.

Further, as per Ex.R.3 driving licence, the driver of offending goods vehicle was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle, bearing licence No.KA-18- 19870000071, Badge No.3271/BUS,
valid till 14-12-2025.
In such circumstances, it can safely be held that, there is no breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-54-6940 the said accident has occurred and the deceased has succumbed to grievous injuries sustained in the said accident.

sentences.text: Though the respondent No.2 has taken the above contention in its written statement, it has failed to establish the same.

Except the self serving statements of R.W.1, who is the representative/Manager Claims of respondent No.2 insurance company, there is no other oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2 to establish that, at the relevant point of time of accident the deceased was traveling in the offending Ashok Leyland goods vehicle bearing No.KA-54-6940 as a passenger.

On the other hand, the representative of respondent No.2/R.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, at the time of accident the offending vehicle was hired by the builders of Prestige Golf Square, Bengaluru, for transportation of construction materials.

Further, the respondent No.1/R.W.1 has himself clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, he was carrying the 'L' angles/goods of the hirer in the offending vehicle and the deceased was sitting in the back cabin by holding the said 'L' angles.
This clearly goes to show that, the deceased was traveling in the offending goods vehicle along with the goods, in the capacity of authorised representative of owner of goods.

The Sec.147 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, mandates insurance policies to cover liability for the death or bodily injury of any person, including the owner of the goods or their authorised representative.

In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 insurance company cannot deny its obligation to indemnify the insured in respect of compensation to be paid to the petitioners, who are the legal representatives of deceased authorised representative of the owner of goods, being transported in the insured Ashok Leyland goods vehicle bearing No.KA-54-6940.

The said provision reads as follows:
147. Requirements of policies and limits of liability - (1) In order to comply with the requirements of this Chapter, a policy of insurance must be a policy which - (a) is issued by a person who is an authorised insurer; and (b) insures the person or classes of persons specified in the policy to the extent specified in sub- section (2) -
(i) against any liability which may be incurred by him in respect of the death of or bodily injury to any person including owner of the goods or his authorised representative carried in the motor vehicle or damage to any property of a third party caused by or arising out of the use of the motor vehicle in a public place;
(ii) against the death of or bodily injury to any passenger of a transport vehicle, except gratuitous passengers of a goods vehicle, caused by or arising out of the use of the motor vehicle in a public place.
29.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of M/S National Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s Balajit Kaur and others, reported in 2004(2) SCC 1, has clearly held that, "It is therefore, manifest that inspite of the amendment of 1994, the effect of the provision contained in Section 147 with respect to persons Kusum Kumari vs Rizwan Pasha on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15880027/
11 other than the owner of the goods or his authorized representative remains the same.

sentences.text: Although the owner of the goods or his authorized representative would now be covered by the policy of insurance in respect of a goods vehicle, it was not the intention of the legislature to provide for the liability of the insurer with respect to passengers, especially gratuitous passengers, who were neither contemplated at the time the contract of insurance was entered into, nor any premium was paid to the extent of the benefit of insurance to such category of people."

30. Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision and in the light of above provision and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.34,00,800/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization (excluding interest on future prospects amount of Rs.8,92,800/-) from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.34,00,800/- (Rupees thirty four lakh and eight hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation (excluding interest on future prospects amount of Rs.8,92,800/-).
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioners.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

The above compensation amount is apportioned as follows:
Petitioner No.1 - Wife - 20% Petitioner No.2 - Son - 20% Petitioner No.3 - Daughter - 20% Petitioner No.4 - Daughter - 20% Petitioner No.5 - Father - 20%

Out of total compensation amount awarded in favour of petitioner No.1 & 5, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in their name as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in her favour, through e-payment on proper identification and verification.

The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest awarded in favour of petitioners No.2 to 4, shall be deposited in their names as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank, till they attain the age of majority.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
